Bacterial_Leaf_Scorch.quote: Symptoms typically appear in mid to late summer on lower branches as irregular marginal browning on interior leaves.

Botryosphaeria_Rots_And_Cankers.quote: Diplodia quercina kills small branches (usually those less than 1 inch, but up to 4 inches in diameter), causing leaves to turn brown, wilt, die, and remain attached in the canopy.

Ganoderma_Root_And_Butt_Rot.quote: Ganoderma sessile can be found attacking the roots and lower trunk of infected hardwoods.
Conks occur singly or in overlapping groups, growing from lateral roots several feet away from the tree or directly from the root flare and base of the trunk.
When infections are advanced, general canopy dieback symptoms may be observed or no symptoms of the infection will be visible.

Leaf_Spot.quote: Generally, leaf diseases will appear as orange, yellow, black, or brown spots on the surface or underside of the leaf.

Nectria_Canker.quote: Nectria canker (also known as coral-spot canker) is often readily identifiable due to the orange- to pink-colored pads of fungal tissue that erupt through the bark on infected stems and branches.
Foliage on infected branches may be chlorotic, undersized or prematurely shed as a general canopy dieback develops.

Oak_Wilt.quote: Look for leaves with brown edges and green centers. Leaves will continue browning toward the center and base of the leaf.
If infected in the branch, complete wilting, leaf loss, and tree death can occur in as little as four weeks.
